newsitem.title: UK: EUROPE MUTUAL FUND INFLOWS SURGE IN FIRST HALF.
newsitem.headline: EUROPE MUTUAL FUND INFLOWS SURGE IN FIRST HALF.

text.p: European mutual funds have been heavy buyers in their own domestic equity markets in 1997, investing over $18 billion in the first half, according to a study by JP Morgan.

It said the $18.2 billion of domestic equity investment by French, German, Italian, Spanish and UK mutual funds in the first half compared to $3.1 billion in the first half of 1996, and $8.6 billion for 1996 as a whole.
June inflows came in at $2.02 billion, slightly off May's $2.21 billion.
The strong first half came despite outflows from French equity SICAVs, which saw net redemptions of 1.3 billion francs in the first half.
It said German data, a month behind the rest of Europe, confirmed the recent pattern of sustained investment into equities, with a strong bias to international equities.

Italian domestic equity mutual funds attracted 63 billion lira in June, and 1.5 trillion for the first half, while Spanish domestic equity funds attracted a reduced 71 billion peseta in June, but for the first half the net inflow was 917 billion pesetas.

The report by analysts Gary Dugan and Caroline Meroz said the totals for France and Italy in the first half were an improvement on the previous year, but failed to reflect the strong performance of their domestic equity markets.
UK domestic equity funds pulled in a net 527 million stg in June, bringing to 4.2 billion stg the amount taken in the first half. This compares to 4.4 billion stg for the whole of 1996.

The report said international funds showed strong inflows, confirming support for equities across Europe. French investors again showed a preference for the international equity category, which took in 2.8 billion francs in June.
Net flows to Italian international equity funds jumped to a five year high of 2.8 trillion lira in June, more than doubling May's figure.

French fixed income SICAVs saw net outflows of 1.4 billion francs in June, bringing to 4.1 billion the total outflow for the first half. Flows into German bond funds also slowed to 1.2 billion marks in May from 3.9 billion a month earlier.

The report shows asset allocation in German funds tending further towards equities in May, with bonds accounting for 61.9 percent of fund portfolios against 67.1 percent in 1996 and 70.5 percent in 1995. The portfolio model excludes cash allocations.
